summary: Build a visual language from a small vocabulary of geometric relationships with an explicit distinction between metaphor and measured quantities.
objective: Viewers can distinguish a decorative relationship from a labeled data mapping, and overlapping forms do not hide the main structure.
intent_signals: Compose a visual language from repeated shapes
example_prompts: Create a geometric-abstract sculpture of an agent network with an explicit legend for each shape.

principles: Build a visual language from a small vocabulary of geometric relationships with an explicit distinction between metaphor and measured quantities.
implementation: Repeat and vary primitives through scale, interval and orientation; when shapes encode entities, keep identity stable across views.
Use material and light contrast to separate groups rather than adding ornamental texture to every primitive.
Offer a view that reveals the organizing relation; animate transformations or group movement with clear state ownership.

Drive the whole field from three numbers - spacing 0.8 m, scale ratio 1.15 per step, yaw 12 degrees per step - and expose them as named controls; a rule with more than three parameters stops reading as a rule.

Build the field as one InstancedMesh and tint at most 5% of instances with setColorAt plus emissiveIntensity 0.6, so the single exception survives a grayscale screenshot while the rest stays inside one value band.
observable_checks: Viewers can distinguish a decorative relationship from a labeled data mapping, and overlapping forms do not hide the main structure.

defaults.rationale: Geometric abstraction reads when the viewer can infer the rule and then see it broken, so the numbers hold the repeated field inside one narrow value band at 45% saturation and give the single exception both hue and emissive headroom. A 32-degree lens and a 4:1 key at 50 degrees elevation are chosen so identical primitives still present three distinct face values, which is what keeps a field of cubes from collapsing into a flat pattern.

palette.role: accent, the element that breaks the rule

values.value_structure: 55/30/15 dark/mid/light; the repeated field stays inside one value band so the single rule-breaking form reads first
values.saturation_rule: two hue families (blue structure, amber accent); repeated elements <= 45% HSL, the accent <= 80% and applied to at most 5% of instances

lights.ratio: key:fill ~ 4:1 so a cube shows three clearly separated face values and the field reads as volume rather than pattern

values.intensity_unit: three-intensity (lux-scaled for Directional/Hemisphere, candela for Point/Spot; tuned with the stated tone_mapping.exposure)

materials.notes: one shared material for the whole field with per-instance colour through InstancedMesh.setColorAt; the accent instance also carries emissive 0.6 so it survives desaturation

values.signature_technique: one interval rule - spacing 0.8 m, scale x1.15 per step, 12 degrees yaw per step - applied to a single primitive and broken exactly once
never: a uniform square grid unless the subject genuinely is a grid
letting a decorative arrangement imply a measured quantity

known_limits: Values are authored starting points tuned for ACESFilmic tone mapping at exposure 1.0; re-tune every intensity, fog density and bloom threshold if you change the tone mapping or exposure.
No renderer run for this record; values are authored starting points.
creative_affordances: Combine with generative rules or monochrome study; geometry used as metaphor does not become proof of a mathematical claim.
